spec.description: Single-switch operational dashboard for SONiC Exporter. It covers switch identity, host health, interfaces, queues, hardware, optics, ASIC capacity, topology, containers, FDB state, platform health, storage, and exporter diagnostics. Platform-dependent panels can show no data when the related collector or metric is not available.

spec.title: FDB Entries
spec.description: Shows the current number of forwarding database entries learned by the switch. Use it to spot sudden growth, loss of learned MAC addresses, or pressure on FDB capacity.

spec.title: FDB Unknown VLAN
spec.description: Shows FDB entries whose VLAN could not be mapped by the collector. Any non-zero value can indicate incomplete or unexpected source data and should be investigated.

spec.title: FDB Skipped Entries
spec.description: Shows how many FDB entries were omitted during the latest collector refresh. Any non-zero value means the exported FDB view may be incomplete.

spec.title: FDB Truncated
spec.description: Shows whether the FDB collector reached its configured entry limit. Yes means the total or per-port, per-VLAN, and per-type detail can be incomplete.

spec.title: FDB Entries by Port
spec.description: Shows the 20 ports or LAGs with the most learned FDB entries over time. Use it to find where MAC addresses are concentrated and to spot learning changes.

spec.title: FDB Entries by VLAN
spec.description: Shows the 20 VLANs with the most learned FDB entries over time. Use it to identify segments with unusual MAC growth or loss.

spec.title: FDB Entries by Type
spec.description: Shows FDB entries grouped by entry type, such as dynamic or static. Use it to understand the learning mix and notice an unexpected change in type.

spec.title: FDB vs ASIC CRM
spec.description: Compares the FDB collector count with the ASIC CRM fdb_entry usage and shows their difference. Use it to detect skipped entries, timing differences, or disagreement between the software and ASIC views.

spec.title: Switch Identity
spec.description: Shows the switch hostname, platform, model, serial number, and ASIC details. Use it to confirm that the selected target is the device you intend to investigate.

spec.title: SONiC Version
spec.description: Shows the installed SONiC, Debian, kernel, release, branch, and build details. Use it to compare software versions and confirm the build running on the switch. No data is expected when the System collector is disabled.

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Shows how long the switch has been running. It uses the SONiC uptime metric when available and falls back to the host boot time. A sudden reset can confirm a recent reboot.

spec.title: Collector Health
spec.description: Shows OK only when all 14 collector families expected by this dashboard are present and their latest refresh succeeded. Use it as a quick check that the dashboard data is complete. Deployments with optional collectors disabled will show Degraded.

spec.title: CPU Usage
spec.description: Shows the percentage of host CPU time currently in use. Sustained high usage can slow control-plane services or metric collection.

spec.title: Memory Usage
spec.description: Shows the percentage of host memory in use, based on Linux MemAvailable. Use it to spot memory pressure before services are affected.

spec.title: Host Filesystem Used
spec.description: Shows the used percentage of the host filesystem mounted at /host. Use it to catch low disk space that can affect logs, containers, or switch services.

spec.title: Operational Links
spec.description: Shows how many exported interfaces are operationally up and how many are exported in total. Use it as a quick link-count check. Unused breakout lanes can be down without indicating a fault.

spec.title: Max ASIC Resource Used
spec.description: Shows the highest used percentage across valid CRM and ACL hardware resources. Use it to find the ASIC resource closest to exhaustion before new routes, neighbors, or ACL entries fail.

spec.title: PSU Health
spec.description: Shows Healthy when every reported PSU is present and operational. A reported missing or down PSU makes the value Bad. No data means PSU status metrics are not available.

spec.title: FDB Aging Time
spec.description: Shows the configured FDB aging time in seconds. Use it to confirm how long inactive dynamic MAC entries remain before they are removed.

spec.title: Ordered ECMP
spec.description: Shows whether ordered ECMP is enabled. Use it to confirm the forwarding setting expected by the network design; enabled and disabled are both valid configurations.

spec.title: Hash Seeds
spec.description: Shows the configured ECMP and LAG hash seeds. Use it to compare switches and confirm that traffic-distribution settings are consistent where required.

spec.title: Hash Offsets
spec.description: Shows platform-dependent ECMP and LAG hash offsets. Use it to compare traffic-distribution settings when the ASIC exports them. No data is expected on platforms that do not provide these metrics.

spec.title: Fan Health
spec.description: Shows Healthy when every reported fan is present and operational. A reported missing or down fan makes the value Bad. No data means fan status metrics are not available.

spec.title: Temperature Summary
spec.description: Shows the highest non-zero ASIC temperature and the highest reported optic temperature. Use it to identify thermal risk quickly. Unsupported zero readings are ignored.

spec.title: Optic Lanes Reporting
spec.description: Counts the RX and TX optical-power lane series currently reported. Use it to confirm that digital optical monitoring data is being exported for the selected optic.

spec.title: FDB Entries
spec.description: Shows the current number of forwarding database entries. Use it to spot sudden changes in learned MAC addresses.

spec.title: Platform Health
spec.description: Shows Healthy only when the Platform collector succeeds and SYSTEM_HEALTH_INFO contains no non-OK records. Use it to surface system health issues reported by SONiC.

spec.title: Platform Data Complete
spec.description: Shows Complete only when the Platform collector succeeded, skipped zero entries, and did not truncate its results. Use it to decide whether platform health and storage details can be trusted.

spec.expr:
(sonic_platform_collector_success{job="$job",instance="$instance"} == bool 1)
* on(job, instance)
(sonic_platform_entries_skipped{job="$job",instance="$instance"} == bool 0)
* on(job, instance)
(sonic_platform_entries_truncated{job="$job",instance="$instance"} == bool 0)

spec.title: Minimum Storage Health
spec.description: Shows the lowest vendor-reported storage health percentage across devices. Use it to find the weakest storage device quickly. No data means storage health is not exported on this platform.

spec.title: Maximum Storage Temperature
spec.description: Shows the highest reported storage temperature. Use it to identify a hot storage device before reliability is affected. No data means storage temperature is not exported on this platform.

spec.title: Collector Success
spec.description: Shows a timeline of success or failure for each of the 14 SONiC collector families used by this dashboard. Use it to identify which data source failed and when the failure started.

spec.title: Collector Scrape Duration
spec.description: Shows how long each SONiC collector takes to refresh its data. Use it to find slow collectors, command timeouts, or increasing collection cost.

spec.title: Cache Age
spec.description: Shows the age of cached data for every cached collector used by this dashboard. A steadily rising value can mean that a collector has stopped refreshing even if Prometheus can still scrape the exporter.

spec.title: Entries Skipped
spec.description: Shows how many records each collector skipped during its latest refresh. Zero is expected. A non-zero value means some exported detail is incomplete.

spec.title: Entries Truncated
spec.description: Shows whether collectors with entry limits truncated their latest results. Zero is expected. A non-zero value means the detailed view may be incomplete.

spec.title: Docker Source Stale
spec.description: Shows whether the SONiC DOCKER_STATS source is fresh or stale. Use it to separate an exporter problem from stale container data produced by the switch.

spec.title: Node Exporter Collector Success
spec.description: Shows a success timeline for each enabled node exporter collector. Use it to identify host metric families that failed to collect.

spec.title: Platform Health Issues
spec.description: Lists detailed non-OK records from SONiC SYSTEM_HEALTH_INFO. Use it to see the reported reason behind a Platform Health failure. No rows means no detailed issue record was exported, not necessarily that collection was complete.

spec.title: Platform Entries Skipped
spec.description: Shows how many platform-health or storage records were omitted during the latest refresh. Any non-zero value means the detailed platform view is incomplete.

spec.title: Platform Entries Truncated
spec.description: Shows whether the Platform collector reached its configured entry limit. Yes means health or storage details can be missing.

spec.title: Platform Cache Age
spec.description: Shows the age of the latest cached platform-health refresh. Use it to confirm that platform health and storage data are still updating.

spec.title: Platform Scrape Duration
spec.description: Shows how long the Platform collector takes to refresh health and storage data. Use it to detect slow platform commands or collection timeouts.

spec.title: Storage Inventory
spec.description: Lists storage devices with model, firmware, and serial information from STORAGE_INFO. Use it to confirm storage inventory. No data means the platform does not export this information or the collector is disabled.

spec.title: Storage Health
spec.description: Shows vendor-reported storage media health for each device. Use it to identify wear or a degrading device. This is not filesystem free space.

spec.title: Storage Temperature
spec.description: Shows reported storage temperature for each device over time. Use it to identify a hot device or cooling problem. Some platforms provide inventory or health without temperature.

spec.title: Storage Reserved Blocks
spec.description: Shows the raw reserved-block value reported for each storage device. Use it for device-specific wear analysis. No generic alarm threshold is applied because the meaning and scale depend on the device.

spec.title: Storage Disk I/O Rates
spec.description: Shows per-second changes in the storage disk I/O read and write counters. Use it to see device activity and compare read and write demand. No data means these STORAGE_INFO counters are not exported.

spec.title: Storage FSIO Rates
spec.description: Shows per-second changes in the storage total FSIO read and write counters. Use it to see filesystem I/O activity reported by the platform. No data means these STORAGE_INFO counters are not exported.

spec.title: Interface State
spec.description: Shows the administrative and operational state of every interface, together with speed and interface identity. Use it to find links that are enabled but down and to confirm expected port configuration.

spec.expr:
(8 * sonic_interface_speed_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance"})
* on(job, instance, device)
  group_left(alias, description, index)
  sonic_interface_info{job="$job",instance="$instance"}

spec.title: Top RX Throughput
spec.description: Shows the 12 interfaces receiving the most traffic in bits per second. It removes zero, invalid, and physically impossible rates. Use it to find busy ingress links quickly.

spec.title: Top TX Throughput
spec.description: Shows the 12 interfaces sending the most traffic in bits per second. It removes zero, invalid, and physically impossible rates. Use it to find busy egress links quickly.

spec.title: Top RX Utilization
spec.description: Shows the 12 interfaces with the highest receive utilization as a percentage of their configured speed. Use it to identify links approaching capacity. Invalid rates are removed and valid values are capped at 100%.

spec.title: Top TX Utilization
spec.description: Shows the 12 interfaces with the highest transmit utilization as a percentage of their configured speed. Use it to identify links approaching capacity. Invalid rates are removed and valid values are capped at 100%.

spec.title: Interface Packet Mix
spec.description: Shows non-zero receive and transmit packet rates by packet method for the busiest interfaces. Use it to understand whether traffic is unicast, multicast, or broadcast and to spot changes in traffic mix.

spec.title: Interface Errors / Discards / Pause
spec.description: Shows non-zero receive and transmit errors, discards, drops, and pause events per second. Use it to identify interfaces that are losing traffic or experiencing congestion or physical problems.

spec.title: RX Ethernet Frame Sizes
spec.description: Shows the busiest receive frame-size buckets per interface. Use it to understand packet-size distribution, which helps explain packet rate, overhead, and workload changes.

spec.title: TX Ethernet Frame Sizes
spec.description: Shows the busiest transmit frame-size buckets per interface. Use it to understand packet-size distribution, which helps explain packet rate, overhead, and workload changes.

spec.title: Top Queue Throughput
spec.description: Shows the queues carrying the most traffic in bits per second. Use it to identify which egress queues are busy and whether traffic is concentrated in a particular class. Impossible aggregate rates are filtered out.

spec.title: Top Queue Packet Rates
spec.description: Shows the queues carrying the most packets per second. Use it to find high packet-rate queues that may stress buffering or scheduling even when bit rate is moderate.

spec.title: Queue Drop Packet Rates
spec.description: Shows only queues with a non-zero packet-drop rate. Use it to find active congestion and identify the affected interface and queue.

spec.expr:
topk(16,
  (rate(sonic_queue_dropped_packets_total{job="$job",instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(job, instance, device) group_left(alias, description) sonic_interface_info{job="$job",instance="$instance"})
  and on(job, instance, device, queue) (rate(sonic_queue_dropped_packets_total{job="$job",instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) > 0)
)

spec.title: Queue Drop Bit Rates
spec.description: Shows only queues with a non-zero dropped-byte rate, converted to bits per second. Use it to measure the traffic volume lost to queue congestion.

spec.expr:
topk(16,
  ((8 * rate(sonic_queue_dropped_bytes_total{job="$job",instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(job, instance, device) group_left(alias, description) sonic_interface_info{job="$job",instance="$instance"})
  and on(job, instance, device, queue) (rate(sonic_queue_dropped_bytes_total{job="$job",instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) > 0)
)

spec.title: Persistent Queue Watermarks
spec.description: Shows the latest non-zero persistent shared queue watermark values. Use it to identify queues that have reached the greatest buffer use. The panel intentionally displays the reported watermark value rather than a rate.

spec.expr:
topk(20,
  (sonic_queue_watermark_bytes_total{job="$job",instance="$instance",type="persistent",watermark="shared"} * on(job, instance, device) group_left(alias, description) sonic_interface_info{job="$job",instance="$instance"})
  and on(job, instance, device, queue, type, watermark) (sonic_queue_watermark_bytes_total{job="$job",instance="$instance",type="persistent",watermark="shared"} > 0)
)

spec.title: PSU Inventory
spec.description: Lists the installed power supplies with slot, model, and serial information. Use it to confirm hardware inventory and identify the correct unit during replacement or support work.

spec.title: PSU Status
spec.description: Shows the operational and availability state of each power supply. Use it to distinguish a failed PSU from one that is not present.

spec.title: Fan Reported Speed
spec.description: Shows the fan speed value reported by the platform for each chassis and PSU fan. Use it to spot a stopped fan or a sudden change. The unit is left generic because some platforms report chassis fans on a different scale from PSU fans.

spec.title: Fan Status
spec.description: Shows the operational and availability state of each fan. Use it to distinguish a failed fan from one that is not present.

spec.title: ASIC Temperature
spec.description: Shows current, average, and maximum ASIC temperature readings when available. Use it to detect overheating and compare current conditions with the platform summary. Unsupported zero readings are hidden.

defaults.noValue: If no data, then all metrics are 0

spec.title: PSU Voltage
spec.description: Shows voltage reported by each power supply. Use it to compare redundant PSUs and spot unstable or abnormal input. No data means this telemetry is not available on the platform.

spec.title: PSU Current
spec.description: Shows current reported by each power supply. Use it to compare load sharing between redundant PSUs and spot an unusual imbalance. No data means this telemetry is not available on the platform.

spec.title: PSU Power
spec.description: Shows power reported by each power supply. Use it to understand switch power demand and compare load sharing between redundant PSUs. No data means this telemetry is not available on the platform.

spec.title: PSU Temperature
spec.description: Shows temperature reported by each power supply. Use it to find a hot PSU or cooling problem. No data means this telemetry is not available on the platform.

spec.title: Transceiver Reported Status
spec.description: Shows the raw 0/1 transceiver status together with module identity and interface alias. Use it to confirm which optics are reported and whether their status is active.

spec.title: Active Transceiver Alarms / Faults
spec.description: Shows only non-zero transceiver fault, alarm, warning, RX loss-of-signal, and disable flags. Use it as a focused fault list. No data normally means no active flags were exported.

spec.expr:
(sonic_transceiver_status_value{job="$job",instance="$instance",field=~".*(fault|alarm|warning|rxlos|disable).*"} != 0)
* on(job, instance, device) group_left(alias, description, index) sonic_interface_info{job="$job",instance="$instance"}

spec.title: Optic RX Power With DOM Thresholds
spec.description: Shows receive optical power for every reported lane together with the matching DOM warning and alarm limits. Use it to find weak or excessive receive power and judge it against the optic's own thresholds.

spec.title: Optic TX Power With DOM Thresholds
spec.description: Shows transmit optical power for every reported lane together with the matching DOM warning and alarm limits. Use it to find weak or excessive transmit power and judge it against the optic's own thresholds.

spec.title: Optic Temperature With DOM Thresholds
spec.description: Shows optic temperature together with the matching DOM warning and alarm limits. Use it to identify an optic running outside its supported range. No data is expected when the platform does not export per-interface optic temperature.

spec.title: Optic Voltage With DOM Thresholds
spec.description: Shows optic supply voltage together with the matching DOM warning and alarm limits. Use it to identify an optic receiving abnormal voltage. No data is expected when the platform does not export per-interface optic voltage.

spec.title: Transceiver Module Metadata
spec.description: Lists transceiver module state and any reported fault cause, joined to the interface alias. Use it to connect a module-level problem to the physical port an operator knows.

spec.expr: sonic_transceiver_module_info{job="$job",instance="$instance",module_state!=""} * on(job, instance, device) group_left(alias, description, index) sonic_interface_info{job="$job",instance="$instance"}

spec.title: DOM Threshold Values
spec.description: Lists all exported digital optical monitoring threshold values by device and threshold name. Use it as a reference when investigating an alarm or comparing optic limits.

spec.title: CRM Resource Used Percent
spec.description: Shows used percentage for each supported CRM hardware resource. Use it to find route, neighbor, next-hop, FDB, or other ASIC tables that are approaching capacity. Unsupported 0/0 resources are excluded.

spec.title: CRM Resources Used / Available
spec.description: Shows raw used and available values for every CRM resource. Use it to verify the percentage view and understand the absolute remaining capacity.

spec.title: CRM ACL Used Percent
spec.description: Shows used percentage for each supported ACL resource and target. Use it to find ACL table or group capacity that is approaching exhaustion. Unsupported 0/0 combinations are excluded.

spec.title: CRM ACL Used / Available
spec.description: Shows raw used and available ACL values by target and resource. Use it to verify ACL percentages and understand the absolute remaining capacity.

spec.title: L2 Topology Summary
spec.description: Shows summary counts for LLDP neighbors, VLANs, LAGs, and LAG members. Use it to notice a sudden topology or configuration change before opening the detailed tables.

spec.title: LLDP Neighbor Table
spec.description: Lists LLDP neighbors with local interface, remote system, remote port, management address, and chassis identity. Use it to verify physical connections and find the remote end of a link.

spec.title: VLAN Member Counts
spec.description: Shows the current member count for each VLAN. Use it to spot an unexpected loss or growth of VLAN membership.

spec.title: VLAN Admin State
spec.description: Shows the administrative state of each VLAN. Use it to confirm that required VLANs are enabled. The exporter does not provide a separate VLAN operational-state metric here.

spec.title: LAG Member Counts
spec.description: Shows the configured member count for each link aggregation group. Use it to spot a missing member or an unexpected configuration change.

spec.title: LAG Admin / Oper State
spec.description: Shows administrative and operational state for each link aggregation group. Use it to find a LAG that is enabled in configuration but not operational.

spec.title: LAG Member Status
spec.description: Shows the status of every member in each link aggregation group. Use it to identify the specific physical interface causing reduced LAG capacity or resilience.

spec.title: VLAN Membership Table
spec.description: Lists every VLAN-to-interface membership and its tagging mode. Use it to verify access and trunk membership during configuration or forwarding investigations.

spec.title: Host CPU by Mode
spec.description: Shows the average percentage of CPU time spent in each Linux mode. Use it to distinguish user load, kernel work, I/O wait, soft interrupts, and idle time.

spec.title: Host CPU Usage by CPU
spec.description: Shows busy percentage for each logical CPU. Use it to find an uneven workload or a single CPU that is saturated while the overall average looks normal.

spec.title: Host Load Average
spec.description: Shows the Linux 1, 5, and 15 minute load averages. Use it to see whether runnable or blocked work is a short spike or a sustained condition.

spec.title: Host Memory Available / Total
spec.description: Shows available and total host memory. Use it to see remaining memory in bytes and compare it with the percentage summary.

spec.title: Host Filesystem Used Percent
spec.description: Shows used percentage for the host filesystem mounted at /host. Use it to monitor the real host filesystem without duplicate container bind mounts.

spec.title: Disk Read / Write Throughput
spec.description: Shows read and write throughput per physical disk. Use it to identify storage activity or an I/O-heavy event. Loop, RAM, and optical devices are excluded.

spec.title: Disk IOPS
spec.description: Shows completed read and write operations per second for each physical disk. Use it to identify high I/O request rates separately from byte throughput.

spec.title: Disk Busy Percent
spec.description: Shows the percentage of time each physical disk is busy, capped at 100%. Use it to identify a saturated storage device even when throughput is not high.

spec.title: Context Switches / Interrupts
spec.description: Shows context switches and interrupts per second. Use it to spot unusual kernel activity that can accompany packet load, driver problems, or process churn.

spec.title: Docker Containers
spec.description: Shows the number of containers present in SONiC DOCKER_STATS. Use it as a quick inventory check and to notice missing or newly added services.

spec.title: Docker Source Age
spec.description: Shows how old the source DOCKER_STATS data is. Use it to tell whether container values are current even when the exporter itself is still responding.

spec.title: Docker Source Stale
spec.description: Shows whether SONiC marks the DOCKER_STATS source as stale. Use it to avoid trusting container values that are no longer being refreshed.

spec.title: Container Inventory
spec.description: Lists every container reported by SONiC DOCKER_STATS. Use it to confirm service inventory and the exact container names used by the other panels.

spec.title: Container CPU
spec.description: Shows the ten containers with the highest non-zero CPU percentage. Values can exceed 100% when a container uses more than one CPU. Use it to find CPU-heavy services quickly.

spec.title: Container Memory Percent
spec.description: Shows the ten containers with the highest non-zero memory percentage. Use it to find services consuming the largest share of host memory.

spec.title: Container Memory Usage
spec.description: Shows the ten containers with the highest non-zero memory use in bytes. Use it to compare absolute memory demand when percentage limits are similar or misleading.

spec.title: Container PIDs
spec.description: Shows the ten containers with the highest non-zero process counts. Use it to spot process growth, a fork problem, or an unexpectedly complex service.

spec.title: Container Block I/O
spec.description: Shows non-zero container block read and write rates. Use it to find services generating storage activity or log pressure.

spec.title: SONiC Exporter
